objective.statement: Choose between adopting, adapting and building a capability, with the existing prior art fully enumerated BEFORE any build option is scored.
objective.charter: MANDATE. The ordering is the rule: prior art is enumerated first, and only then may a build option be scored. Score the build first and every subsequent comparison is anchored on it - the team has already imagined the thing, so adoption starts the race behind. Enumeration must include the option nobody enjoys proposing: that a native feature already covers the need and the correct action is to ENABLE something rather than author a new file. Candidates are compared pairwise so 'adopt beats build' is a recorded comparison rather than a mood, and the owner breaks a genuine tie because adopt-versus-build is ultimately a question about what the owner wants to maintain.
success_criteria: prior art enumerated and timestamped before any build option is scored
the enable-a-native-feature option is explicitly considered and dispositioned
at least three sources gathered during enumeration
every pairwise comparison recorded, with the owner breaking ties

forbidden_actions: score a build option before prior art is enumerated
declare a capability absent without searching for it
author a new file where enabling an existing feature suffices

context.briefing: Block any scoring of a build option until enumeration is closed. Before anyone declares a capability missing, make them search for it - the dominant measured failure is recall, not detection: the thing was already built and simply unread.

roster.display_name: Cost analyst - total cost including the catalogue tax
Architect - fit with what already exists
Critic - argues for the option the room likes least

context.briefing: Steelman the least popular option, especially 'enable what exists and write nothing'. If the room converges fast on building, that is your cue, not your consensus.

roster.display_name: Owner representative - breaks ties, owns the maintenance

sequence.custom_name: enumerate prior art and native features BEFORE any build option is scored
pairwise comparison of adopt / adapt / build / enable-existing

conditional_decision_requires: if the ranking selects build, a time-boxed spike proves the adopt option genuinely fails first

metadata.title: Skill adoption versus build (advisory, owner tie-break)
metadata.notes: SOURCE DESIGN: C-H64 `skill-adoption-vs-build`, global ordinal 64, tier standard, protocols P37/P28, 6 seats, 2 rounds, default binding ADVISORY, OWNER-DECISION YES. This is the LAST design-derived preset in lane build/preset-4; ordinals 65-72 of the doc (C-H65..C-H72) fall outside the program's 64-preset budget and are NOT built by any lane - reported, not silently dropped. || EDITABLE DIALS: (1) prior_art_scope -> the enumerate-prior-art stage, preparation.min_sources (3) and the sources_gathered stopping clause; widening the scope is cheap and is where this council earns its keep. Secondary dials: budgets.time_minutes (45), topology.tournament.aggregation (copeland), voting.tie_break (owner), consensus.threshold (0.7). || VOCABULARY MAP (design term -> CouncilSpec enum): voting `pairwise_then_owner` -> topology.kind `pairwise_tournament` (round_robin, copeland) plus voting.method `condorcet` with tie_break `owner`; the pairwise half is topology and the owner half is the tie-break. roles `methodologist` -> custom:methodologist as chair, `implementer` -> custom:implementer, `cost_analyst` -> custom:cost_analyst, `architect` -> architect (enum), `critic` -> devils_advocate (enum, chosen over `critic` because the seat is briefed to steelman the least popular option rather than attack the leading one), `owner_rep` -> custom:owner_rep (kind human, vendor human, authority owner). Outcomes map CONSENSUS->decision, MAJORITY_WITH_DISSENT->dissent, INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE->no_decision, CONDITIONAL_DECISION->conditional_decision, DEFER->no_decision. `evidence standard: assertion_with_pointer` -> anchor_style `any` with citation_required true and min_independent_sources 2. || A DELIBERATE ADDITION BEYOND THE DESIGN: consensus.fast_unanimity_is_suspicious is TRUE here even though the design row says anti-sycophancy off. Fast agreement to BUILD is the specific pathology this council exists to interrupt - it is the enjoyable option and the room converges on it early - so the fast-unanimity response is armed with forced_dissent and blind_re_evaluation. If that is unwanted, this is the field to flip. || CUSTOM METRICS AND THEIR PRODUCERS: custom:prior_art_enumerated_before_scoring (boolean; produced by the chair, and the ORDERING is part of the claim - enumeration timestamps must precede the first build score) and custom:native_feature_option_dispositioned (boolean; produced by the pairwise-score stage, requiring the enable-existing option to be explicitly accepted or rejected with a reason). Producers cannot live on the leaves: SEM-001 compares parse(source_expression) with the tree by dict equality and parse() emits no `producer` key - both-states probe at platform/council/_probe_note_vs_source_expression.py. Two SEM-012 WARNs are expected and non-blocking. || WHY sources_gathered >= 3 IS THE THIRD CLAUSE: it is the registry metric that makes 'we looked' checkable. An enumeration claiming completeness on one source is a recollection, not a search.
